# QR Editor (qr.giit.ch)

> Free QR code generator and editor in the browser, no sign-up, no tracking, codes kept in the browser. Makes static QR codes (no expiry date: the content is in the code, no redirect; a code works as long as its content, e.g. the link, does) for links, text, WiFi, contacts (vCard, MeCard), email, SMS, phone, location, calendar events, crypto payments, SEPA payments (EPC GiroCode) and Swiss QR bills. Design with colors, gradients, module and eye shapes, a logo, caption and frame; the code displayed in the editor is checked at normal, small and blurred sizes; batch exports are not scanned automatically; export SVG, PNG, JPEG, WebP, PDF and EPS; reads QR codes from pictures and the camera; makes many codes at once from a table.

- Language: English at /, 13 other languages at /de/, /fr/, /it/, /es/, /pt/, /nl/, /pl/, /tr/, /ru/, /uk/, /zh/, /ja/, /ko/
- Cost: free
- Data: documents stay in the browser (localStorage) unless the user sets up a webhook to their own server, or a website that embeds the editor receives it (postMessage) and saves it on its own server. Pictures and the camera image read for codes never leave the browser. A document sent to post.php by a form (viewer) is passed to the browser in memory and not stored on the server. The server logs requests (IP address, address requested), and page views are counted anonymously.
- No files of a document: a picture logo is part of the QR document as a data URI; there are no `assets` fields in any message.

## The QR document (.qr)

Plain text: optional design lines `key: value`, a line `---`, then the content exactly as it goes into the code (one final line break is not part of it). Text without such a header is all content, so a plain link is a valid document. Lines starting with `#` in the header are comments.

    color: #1d2b53
    modules: rounded
    logo: wifi
    ecc: Q
    caption: Guest WiFi
    ---
    WIFI:T:WPA;S:Guest;P:sunny-day-42;;

Design keys (all optional, default in brackets): `ecc` L|M|Q|H (M), `boost` yes|no (yes), `version` auto|1-40 (auto), `mask` auto|0-7 (auto), `margin` 0-20 modules (4), `color` #rgb/#rrggbb (#000000), `color2` (none), `gradient` none|linear|radial (none), `angle` 0-360 (45), `background` color or transparent (#ffffff), `modules` square|rounded|dots|soft|diamond|bars-v|bars-h (square), `eye-frame` square|rounded|circle|leaf (square), `eye-ball` square|rounded|circle|diamond|leaf (square), `eye-color` (the dark color), `logo` none|wifi|web|mail|phone|chat|pin|calendar|user|pay|star|heart or `data:image/(png|jpeg|gif|webp|svg+xml);base64,…` (none), `logo-size` 5-30 percent (20), `logo-clear` yes|no (yes), `caption` one line (none), `caption-position` below|above (below), `frame` none|line|filled (none), `frame-color` (the dark color). Unknown keys and invalid values are kept and reported; the default is used.

## Content formats

The type is read from the content: `https://…` link; `WIFI:T:WPA;S:<ssid>;P:<password>;H:true;;` (T:WPA also for WPA3, T:WEP, T:nopass; escape `\ ; , : "`); vCard 3.0 (`BEGIN:VCARD` … `END:VCARD`) or `MECARD:N:Last,First;TEL:…;;`; `mailto:<to>?subject=…&body=…`; `SMSTO:<number>:<text>`; `tel:<number>`; `geo:<lat>,<lon>`; `BEGIN:VEVENT` … `END:VEVENT`; `bitcoin:`/`litecoin:`/`dogecoin:`/`bitcoincash:` (BIP21) and `ethereum:<addr>?value=<wei>` (EIP-681); EPC069-12 SEPA (`BCD`, `002`, `1`, `SCT`, BIC, name, IBAN, `EUR<amount>`, purpose, RF reference or text; at most 331 bytes; error correction M); Swiss QR bill (`SPC`, `0200`, `1`, IBAN CH/LI, structured address `S`, amount, CHF/EUR, debtor, `QRR`/`SCOR`/`NON`, reference, message, `EPD`; drawn with the Swiss cross, error correction M, design lines ignored; EUR only with SCOR or NON). Everything else is text. `{{column}}` placeholders are filled by "Many codes from a table".

## Features

- Code (the QR document), the drawn code and a side panel: Content (the type and its form, writing the content in its canonical form), Design (colors, shapes, logo, caption, frame, error correction), Check.
- Scan check: after each change the code displayed in the editor is read back with jsQR in the browser, normal, small (3 pixels per module) and blurred with less contrast; the result is shown at the code and as a problem. Batch exports are not scanned automatically.
- Payment forms check IBANs, payment references and supported field limits.
- Problems with their line: content too long, contrast below 3:1 (error) or 4.5:1 (warning), light on dark, transparent background, quiet zone below 4 modules, a logo hiding more than the error correction repairs, unknown keys, invalid values, and the checks of each type (IBAN check digits, QR-IBAN only with a QR reference, QR reference check digit, RF creditor reference, EPC length, WiFi password, link shorteners and redirect services).
- Print size: from the scanning distance the smallest size (distance / 10), and the size of one module for a printed width.
- Export: SVG, PNG (64-8192 pixels, dpi written into the file), JPEG, WebP, PDF and EPS (vectors, width in mm, gradients as shadings), the content as text, the .qr document, all in one ZIP; copy as picture.
- Print exports: SVG, PDF and EPS provide scalable QR shapes. Uploaded picture logos and some PDF/EPS captions are raster images. For PNG, choose pixel width and DPI to match the print size.
- Many codes from a table: CSV/TSV with a header row, `{{column}}` in the content and caption, a ZIP of SVG or PNG files (named from a column) or one PDF with a page per row; at most 5000 rows.
- Reading codes: open, drop or paste a picture (PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP, BMP, SVG) or use the camera ("Read code"); light-on-dark codes too. The content becomes a new document.
- Caption edited in place on the drawing.
- My documents: any number of QR documents in the browser, with a picture of each code.

## Writing for a user (for AI assistants)

Any AI can put a QR document into the user's open editor with a link; no server, no API key:

- `https://qr.giit.ch/#b64=<base64url of the UTF-8 QR document>`
- `https://qr.giit.ch/#qr=<URL-encoded QR document>`
- `https://qr.giit.ch/#z=<base64url of the zlib-compressed QR document>` (shorter)
- Add `&file=new&name=<name>` to make a new document next to the user's others, or `&file=<name>` to change that one. Without `&file=` the open document changes.
- Long documents (a picture logo): split the encoded text and send one link per part with `&part=N&of=M&id=<name>`.

Write the complete QR document; keep the dark color dark and the background light. The user can undo every change. In the editor, "AI Assistant" > "Copy prompt" gives the AI these instructions together with the current document.

## Saving on your own server (webhook)

Set under "Save to server" (cloud button), or for one document with `?webhook=<URL>`: only for that one document and only while the page is open - a link never stores a webhook. At the top level the user is asked first; inside a page (iframe or opener) it only works together with `?src=` and only for the document opened with it. On "Save" (Ctrl+S), or automatically a few seconds after each change if chosen, the browser sends:

    POST <webhook URL>
    Content-Type: application/json
    Authorization: Bearer <token>        (only if a token is set)

    {"editor":"qr","event":"save","id":"<document id>","name":"<name>",
     "content":"<the QR document>","updated":"<ISO date>"}

One request carries at most 40 MB; the server's error text (e.g. for 413) is shown to the user. The server must answer CORS requests from https://qr.giit.ch (Access-Control-Allow-Origin, and Access-Control-Allow-Headers: Content-Type, Authorization). `?src=<URL>` opens a .qr file (or any text, which becomes the content) from a URL (CORS needed), `&name=<name>` names it. The content is the QR document exactly as it is in the editor: design lines, `---`, the content.

## Embedding in a website

A guide for developers with examples, in every language of the editor: [https://qr.giit.ch/embed/](https://qr.giit.ch/embed/) (`/<code>/embed/`, e.g. `/de/embed/`). The complete protocol follows here.

    <iframe src="https://qr.giit.ch/?embed=1" allow="clipboard-write; camera" style="width:100%;height:80vh;border:0"></iframe>

Messages (postMessage; check `event.origin === "https://qr.giit.ch"` and `event.source === iframe.contentWindow`):

- Editor -> page: `{type:"qreditor:ready", version:2, editor:"qr", window:false}` when it can take a document.
- Page -> editor: `{type:"qreditor:load", name, content}` opens the document (a document of that name from your page is replaced, otherwise made).
- Editor -> page: `{type:"qreditor:loaded", id, name}`, then `{type:"qreditor:change", id, name, content}` on each edit (not after load), and `{type:"qreditor:save", id, name, content, editor, event, updated}` when the user clicks Save or presses Ctrl+S.
- Page -> editor: `{type:"qreditor:get"}` asks for a `qreditor:save` message; `{type:"qreditor:save"}` saves as if the user had clicked Save.

In embedded mode the page text below the editor is hidden and a Save button is shown. The other giit editors (latex.giit.ch, svg.giit.ch and more) speak the same protocol with their own prefix (`latexeditor:`, `svgeditor:` …).

Optional fields of `qreditor:load`:
- `context: {host, title, rules}` - plain text about the page (rules up to 2000 characters). "Copy prompt" in the AI Assistant then tells the AI that the document belongs to that page and is saved back there, includes the rules, and leaves out how to build a webhook server.
- `hook: {url, token}` - a webhook (https) for this document only, used on Save in addition to the message; kept in memory only (never stored, gone on reload). If the server answers with an error, its `{"error": "…"}` (or `message`, or a short text) is shown to the user.

AI Assistant in a frame: add `allow="clipboard-write"` to the iframe so "Copy prompt" can use the clipboard (without it the editor falls back to the old copy command or shows the prompt to copy by hand). Links from an AI cannot reach an editor inside another website (the browser keeps its storage and channels apart), so in a frame the prompt and the dialog ask to paste the AI's whole answer into the editor; use the own window (below) if links should work.

`qreditor:get` is always answered with a `qreditor:save` message, also when nothing changed.

### All messages at a glance

Editor -> page (sent to the page around the editor, or to window.opener in its own window):
- `qreditor:ready` {version:2, editor, window} - can take a document
- `qreditor:loaded` {id, name, target?} - after each load; remember the id (target:"new" for a new document from the AI, which is not yours)
- `qreditor:change` {id, name, content} - a real edit of your document (not after load)
- `qreditor:save` {editor, event, id, name, content, updated} - Save / Ctrl+S (from anywhere in the editor), or the answer to get
- `qreditor:closing` {id, name, unsaved, content?} - own window closes (always sent; content only when unsaved, id null before the first load)
- `qreditor:reload` {id, unsaved} - inside your page, F5 / Ctrl+R / Cmd+R do not reload the editor; ask the user yourself (Ctrl+W cannot be caught by a page)
- `qreditor:key-request` {reason:"missing"} - the editor has no AI key in this session yet

`?embed=1&save=0` hides the editor's Save button (Ctrl+S still sends `qreditor:save`) - for pages with their own Save button.

`?theme=light`, `?theme=dark` or `?theme=auto` (with or without `embed`) fixes the color theme for that page load and hides the theme switch; the user's own stored choice is not changed. Other values are ignored.

The address sets the language of the interface and of the page: `/` English, `/de/` German, `/fr/`, `/it/`, `/es/`, `/pt/`, `/nl/`, `/pl/`, `/tr/`, `/ru/`, `/uk/`, `/zh/`, `/ja/`, `/ko/` (`?lang=xx` leads there); `/` leads to the browser's language, and a language picked in the menu holds for every giit.ch site. The AI prompt is always English.

Page -> editor (only from the page around the editor or the opener; after its first message only from that origin; pages without a real origin are ignored):
- `qreditor:load` {name, content, context?, hook?, ai?, from?, target?} - open your document; from:"ai" shows a note, target:"new" opens it as a separate document in the user's browser
- `qreditor:get` - answered with `qreditor:save` of your document (id and content null before the first load)
- `qreditor:save` - press Save
- `qreditor:ai` {label?, prompt?, endpoint?, key?, base?} or {clear:true} - AI through your server

Your document is the one your page loaded (or opened with ?src=). change, save, closing and get are only ever about it - never about other documents in the user's browser, also when the user opens them in the editor. A load replaces only a document that came from your page before (same name and origin), never the user's own; the AI settings and the hook from load apply only while your document is open. Your document is kept in memory only - it is never stored in the user's browser and is gone when the editor closes.

### AI through your own server (prompt and session key)

The editor has no backend; your site keeps the keys and the results. Hand the editor your prompt, an endpoint and a key for this editor session - in `qreditor:load` as `ai: {…}`, or at any time as its own message:

    {type:"qreditor:ai", label:"Example Admin", prompt:"<your instructions, up to 8000 characters>",
     endpoint:"https://your-site.com/api/ai-result", key:"<session key>",
     base:true}

Fields left out keep their value; `{type:"qreditor:ai", clear:true}` ends it. One key per editor session: once the editor has a key it keeps it until the session ends or `clear`, and does not take a different one. `base:false` leaves out the editor's own instructions. The AI dialog shows "Connected to <label> (<real host>)", what your page tells the AI, and a choice: change the current document (default) or make a new one. "Copy prompt" copies the editor's short instructions, your prompt (fenced, marked with your real host), the current QR document and how to send the result:

    POST <endpoint>
    Authorization: Bearer <key>
    Content-Type: application/json
    {"editor":"qr","target":"current"|"new","name":"<short name>","content":"<the complete QR document>"}

An AI that cannot send HTTP requests answers with a link instead, which the user pastes into the editor. When your server has a result, your page sends `{type:"qreditor:load", name, content, from:"ai", target}`: target "current" (or none) puts it into your document (the user sees a note; Undo takes it back; it counts as not yet saved), target "new" opens a separate document that stays in the user's browser - its edits and Save never go to your page. The key stays valid in the editor for the whole session; only when it has none at "Copy prompt", the editor sends `{type:"qreditor:key-request", reason:"missing"}`; answer with a `qreditor:ai` message within 5 seconds.

Safety built in: key, endpoint and prompt are only taken from the page around the editor (after its first message, only from that origin), kept in memory, never stored and never sent by the editor itself - the key only goes into the prompt the user copies. The endpoint must be https on your page's own host (with or without www.) or a subdomain of it; others are refused. Keys must be 16-512 characters of A-Z a-z 0-9 . _ ~ + / = -.

Your backend should: make keys with at least 128 random bits, store only their hash, bind each key to the logged-in user, the document and this editor session, make exactly one key per session, give it no fixed lifetime but keep it valid only while your open page reports the session (e.g. every minute; void it 3 minutes after the last report), void it when the editor, its window or your page closes and when the user logs out, accept only JSON of a sensible size, keep results as drafts until the user saves in the editor, answer key requests only for the logged-in user, and not send CORS headers on the endpoint (AIs call it from a server or a command line, not from a browser).

### Own window

    const win = window.open("https://qr.giit.ch/?embed=window", "qreditor-<id>");   // no "noopener"

The full editor (not the reduced embedded view) with a Save button, in a top-level window, so links from an AI reach it. It talks to `window.opener` exactly as an iframe talks to its parent: `qreditor:ready` goes to the opener, messages are only taken from it, and once the page has sent a message, answers go only to its origin. Save sends `qreditor:save` to the opener (if it is still open) and to the webhook from `load`. Closing the window always sends `{type:"qreditor:closing", id, name, unsaved}`, with `content` when there are changes that were not saved; if the opener is gone, the browser asks before closing with such changes. When the opener is closed, the AI settings (key included) and the hook from `load` end. Calling `window.open` again with the same name reloads the window - focus the existing one instead. The site sends no Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy, so `window.opener` is kept.

## Tools for browser agents (WebMCP)

In browsers with WebMCP (`document.modelContext`), the editor page registers tools that run in the page itself: `get_document`, `get_problems`, `set_content` (content), `set_design` (key, value; "" removes the key), `set_document` (qr), `scan_check`, `undo`, and `list_files`, `open_file`, `new_file` for the user's other documents. Every change is an undo step for the user.

## Viewer and documents by POST

`?viewer=1` shows only the drawn code with Download and Export, read-only, and stores nothing in the browser. The content comes from a link (`#b64=`, `#qr=`, `#z=`, `?src=`), from `qreditor:load` in an iframe, or by POST.

`POST /post.php?viewer=1` as `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` with `content` (text) or `b64` (base64 or base64url), optional `name` and `lang`, at most 20 MB of text. Without `viewer=1` the document opens in the normal editor, in memory only. The document is not stored on the server.
